feedback.problem: Let $f$ be a function such that ${f}^{′}(x)=(2x-3)^{2}(x-1)^{4}$ and $f(0)=-2.$ Use the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=0$ to estimate the value of $f(1).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $a=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(0)+{f}^{′}(0)(x-0) \\  & =f(0)+{f}^{′}(0)x\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that $f(0)=-2,$ and since ${f}^{′}(x)==(2x-3)^{2}(x-1)^{4},$ then ${f}^{′}(0)==(2(0)-3)^{2}(0-1)^{4}=9.$ So, the tangent line approximation is given by

$$
L(x)=-2+9x.
$$

Now, we can approximate $f(1)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=1.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) & ≈L(1) \\  & =-2+9(1) \\  & =-2+9 \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$
